metadata.name: Filigree Hybrid Scene Bank
metadata.notes: Loose narrative contracts for an earlier Python variant. This bank keeps plot, stats, and player intent in balance without fixed scene cards.

story.style: grounded, local, flexible, consequence-driven one-shot play
premise_seeds: A public place hides a private crisis that is starting to leak into view.
A routine errand, job, or night out turns up evidence of a larger local problem.
A stranger, witness, or rival asks for help while clearly leaving something out.
A damaged object, missing person, or contested place points toward a conflict nobody wants named.
A familiar-looking situation has one detail that refuses to behave normally.
A local authority wants calm more than truth, and that makes the truth harder to reach.
pressure_seeds: Someone benefits if the player mistakes the surface problem for the whole problem.
Waiting makes the cost more visible, but rushing gives someone else leverage.
The safest explanation protects the wrong person.
The player can make progress only by choosing what risk to accept.
Every answer clarifies one problem and exposes another.
A useful ally, witness, or tool comes with a condition attached.
anchor_seeds: one contested location, one wary witness, and one piece of physical evidence
one social relationship under strain, one ticking deadline, and one useful lie
one place everyone overlooks, one person with divided loyalties, and one object out of place
one local rule, one person who breaks it, and one consequence that proves why it exists
movements: Expose the immediate pressure and give the player a concrete first lead.
Let player choices reveal cost, opposition, leverage, and personal stakes.
Bring existing pressure to a decisive local consequence without replacing the premise.
story.possible_ending: Resolve what changes locally, who pays or benefits, and what visible mark the player leaves behind.

stat_guidance.STR: force, leverage, intimidation, direct risk, and what physically gives way
stat_guidance.DEX: speed, timing, stealth, precision, and what almost slips away
stat_guidance.CON: endurance, pain, stamina, restraint, and what it costs to keep going
stat_guidance.INT: deduction, systems, memory, planning, and what the character understands
stat_guidance.WIS: perception, instinct, restraint, danger signs, and what feels wrong
stat_guidance.CHA: presence, persuasion, deception, rapport, and who changes their mind

outcome_contracts.Great success: The player gets what they wanted plus a clear advantage. Reveal useful information, improve position, or reduce immediate pressure.
outcome_contracts.Good success: The player gets what they wanted cleanly. Advance the current situation without adding a major new problem.
outcome_contracts.OK success: The player mostly gets what they wanted. Add a small cost, delay, exposure, or incomplete detail.
outcome_contracts.Slight success: The player barely gets it. Preserve progress, but make the next choice sharper.
outcome_contracts.Slight failure: The action does not fully work, but it leaves a clue, partial progress, or safer fallback.
outcome_contracts.Kinda bad failure: The action fails and creates a local complication. Do not replace the scene.
outcome_contracts.Bad failure: The action fails with a serious immediate cost tied directly to the attempt.
outcome_contracts.Very bad failure: The action fails badly. Escalate through existing stakes, location, or NPCs; do not invent a new premise.

trivial_contracts.1: Minor progress with a wrinkle. Keep the consequence small and playable.
trivial_contracts.2: Modest progress. Add one concrete detail that changes what the player knows or can try next.
trivial_contracts.3: Clean progress. Let the action work and open the next obvious option.
trivial_contracts.4: Strong progress for a simple action. Give a small advantage without resolving the whole scenario.
trivial_contracts.default: The simple action works enough to move the scene forward without changing the core challenge.

situations: a public room pretending nothing is wrong
a private argument spilling into view
a locked or restricted space with a plausible mundane reason
a helpful person who is scared of being seen helping
a familiar routine interrupted by one impossible detail
a local rule everyone follows without explaining
pressures: a witness becoming less willing to talk
evidence that can be lost, damaged, hidden, or misunderstood
a social cost for asking the right question
a safer option that solves the wrong problem
someone trying to turn uncertainty into obedience
details: one object in the wrong place
a repeated phrase from unrelated mouths
a practical obstacle that reveals motive
a sensory detail that confirms the danger is local
a small kindness that changes who can be trusted
a sign of recent cleanup, repair, or concealment
questions: what someone moved before the player arrived
which witness is protecting someone else
why the safest route is suddenly unavailable
what the obvious explanation leaves out
who will pay the cost if the player is right
interruptions: a useful tool fails in a revealing way
the wrong person hears the right sentence
a route closes for a mundane but suspicious reason
a small accident exposes a larger lie

base: You are the Dungeon Master for a fast solo one-shot RPG.
Use concrete, grounded narration. Let the model's own creativity supply staging, dialogue, and texture.
memory_intro: Avoid reusing these recent scene beats unless the player explicitly revisits them:

opening: Open in motion with one place detail, one immediate pressure, and one playable lead.
success: Narrate the result as forward motion, not a new premise.
critical: Resolve the attempted action first. Then show the consequence permitted by the outcome contract.
erratic: Make the interruption surprising but local, playable, and connected to an existing pressure.
conclusion: This is the final narration of the adventure. Close the story definitively. Summarize what was resolved, what cost remains, and what mark the character leaves behind. Do NOT introduce new plot threads, choices, or open-ended situations. Do NOT end with a question or prompt for further action.

length: Do NOT use more than {word_limit} words in your response.
question: Conclude your narrative with only the open-ended question, 'What do you do now?'
